thread:
alex: quick alert — p95 token latency regressed on a subset of m8x7b workloads after yesterday's warmup change. flamegraph: https://perf.internal/fg/2265432100

maria: saw the alert. similar tail on one of our long-chat tests (~3k tokens). looks like stalls during window rollover.

kevin: can you paste the top stack from the flamegraph? wondering if it's the prefetch path or batcher stall.

alex: top of stack is in prefetch_kv_worker -> windowed_prefetch -> try_merge_fragments. snippet:

```\n# latency samples
prefetch_kv_worker  42%\nwindowed_prefetch    31%\ntry_merge_fragments  18%\nkernel_selector      4%\n```\n
sam: interesting — that suggests we spend time merging KV fragments when the sliding window wraps across max_pos. could be fragmentation exponential when RoPE scale shifts the effective positions.

maria: note: the affected traces all hit max_position_embeddings ~16384 boundary then wrap. we recently tweaked RoPE scaling to 1.12 for m8x7b; a small scale change can move wrap points and increase fragment count.

kevin: hypothesis: RoPE scaling + long contiguous prefix causes many small KV tiles to be produced and the merge loop becomes O(n^2) in pathological inputs.

alex: I also see a handful of logs where attention mask calculation returns a partial mask causing batcher to split requests mid-token. sample: `mask_align_mismatch: expected 0/1 but got -1 for seq 4096`

sam: that mask mismatch will force fallback slow-path and disable the fast attention kernel. p95 blows up.

ciara-bot: perf-regression-alert posted for job m8x7b/zone-a (build 2026-03-16_18:02). Suspected area: sliding-window prefetch/merge.

maria: quick mitigation options:
- revert RoPE scale to 1.0 for m8x7b in runtime model map (safe, low-risk)
- short-term: cap prefetch merge iterations to N=8 and fall back to conservative merge (prevents O(n^2))
- longer: make KV tileer produce coalesced tiles when max_pos boundary is near wrap

kevin: I'll run a bisect of the warmup/ropecfg change and validate mask invariants on top 10 failing traces.

sam: i can prototype the merge cap patch. patch is tiny: change `while (frags.size() > 1)` to `for (i=0;i<min(frags.size()-1,8);++i)` and ensure metrics tagged so we can see if we hit the cap.

alex: sounds good. also add a short-circuit: if mask_align_mismatch detected then force `fast_kernel=false` for that request and emit `mask_mismatch=true` metric. we need visibility.

maria: for config: if we revert RoPE scale, we should also bump kv_tile_size from 256->512 for long sessions; fewer tiles = fewer merges. but that impacts batching (bigger tile means more memory per request). tradeoff.

kevin: i'll upload a test harness to replay failing traces with both RoPE scale=1.12 and 1.0, and with/without merge cap. link when done.

sam: quick note on batching heuristics — if a request hits the mask mismatch we should stop coalescing it with others where possible. current batcher merges by age; add a flag `batchable=false` if `mask_mismatch` seen in prefilter. prevents contamination of other requests.

alex: agreed. low-risk rollout: cap merge + metric + batcher opt-out. if that stabilizes p95, we can iterate on tileer changes.

ciara-bot: rollout plan created: 1) merge-cap patch to staging (sam) 2) metrics + fast_kernel short-circuit (alex) 3) RoPE scale revert in model-map (maria) 4) bisect traces (kevin). tagging eng-oncall.

maria: i'll prepare the model-map revert PR targeting canary only. keeps host teams happy.

kevin: bisect results uploaded: https://perf.internal/bisect/2265432100 — culprit seems to be the warmup-rope tweak combined with a tiny change in the prefetch merge ordering.

sam: patch open: https://phab/internal/D1000 — adds merge cap + batcher opt-out + metrics. test run on canary shows p95 back to baseline on replay harness.

alex: thanks. once canary looks good we'll promote. follow-up: add a unit test for mask alignment logic and a replay test for long-window wrap cases.

maria: noted. i'll own the model-map PR and the kv_tile sizing follow-up investigation.

kevin: leaving some TODOs in the bisect doc for owners. ping me if you need the raw traces.

alex: awesome team. I'll close the alert after the canary promotion. :thumbsup:
